messages.subject: ezPerm methods?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Group,

I am using exPerm to do a 1 way anova with repeated measures.  I have
not found documentation pointing to how this works.

I have a treatment and control.  I have 50 subjects, each were
submitted to treatment and control and then a dependent variable
measured on each under both conditions (treatment and control).

I'm assuming that the permutation step "respects" the repeated
measures by swapping individuals between treatment and control but
being sure that each individual is in each.  Here is a toy example
with a small set.

SUBJECT GROUP DEPVAR
1                Treat       0.1
2                 Treat       0.2
3                 Treat       0.3
1                 Control    0.5
2                 Control    0.6
3                 Control    0.7

Then one permutation of the above would be

SUBJECT GROUP DEPVAR
1                Treat       0.5
2                 Treat       0.2
3                 Treat       0.3
1                 Control    0.1
2                 Control    0.6
3                 Control    0.7

Notice that all I did was swap values for subject 1.

Is this at all close?

Thanks,
Seth

messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] ezPerm methods?
messages.body_plain:
The "one within variable" case of the permutation test is the
simplest. It is implemented by computing each subject's difference
score between the conditions, computing the mean difference score,
then doing the following many times:
1) randomly change the sign of each score with a probability of .5
2) recompute the mean and store it

The percentile of the true mean is then computed with respect to the
resulting distribution of simulated means.

messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] ezperm ...within vs between
messages.body_plain:
If you measured the same individuals in each condition, that condition
should definitely be treated as "within", else (1) you lose power and
(2) most functions in ez will fail. The latter is because most ez
functions expect that there is no overlap in wid values between groups
defined by a "between" variable and crash if they encounters overlap.

messages.subject_clean: [ez4r] sorry to bombard the list....but addendum on ezPerm
messages.body_plain:
Most ez functions fail if you tell them to treat a variable as
"between" when it is truly "within". How do they know that the
variable is truly within? The "wid" labels will overlap across levels
of the variable if it is truly between.

If you have a within variable called "really_within"and you want to
explore what would happen if it were treated as between, you need to
create a new wid variable:

my_data$dumID = factor(paste(my_data$realID,my_data$really_within))

then use dumID as the "wid" variable.

messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] Re: ezPerm methods?
messages.body_plain:
In my previous description of what happens with a 2-level within
variable, I described the computation of difference scores and
randomization of their sign. While this is formally equivalent to what
ezPerm does, what ezPerm actually does is slightly more flexible in
that it can deal with 2+ level within variables as well. ezPerm first
computes an F-value for the effect of the within variable, then
repeats the following many times
1) within each person, randomly reassign the condition labels to each data point
2) compute a new anova on the newly labelled data, yielding an F-value
that you keep for later

The percentile of the true F-value is then computed with respect to
the resulting distribution of simulated F-values.

messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] ezANOVA is adequate in this expt.?
messages.subject_clean: [ez4r] ezANOVA is adequate in this expt.?
messages.body_plain:
If your data frame, "my_data", is set up with columns "Individual",
"Treatment", "Time", "VD_value", then you can run:

my_anova = ezANOVA(
    data = my_data
    , dv = .(VD_value)
    , wid = .(Individual)
    , within = .(Treatment,Time)
)
print(my_anova)

However, if you truly have only 5 individuals, you will likely receive
an error message after running the above which will suggest that you
add the "type=1" argument to the call to ezANOVA:

my_anova = ezANOVA(
    data = my_data
    , dv = .(VD_value)
    , wid = .(Individual)
    , within = .(Treatment,Time)
    , type = 1
)
print(my_anova)

Ah, so you'd like to know whether there are differences between the
individuals? In that case, you should probably move to a mixed
modelling context:

#evaluate evidence for a difference between individual intercepts
my_data$dummy = factor(1) #create a dummy variable
restricted_model = lmer(
    formula = VD_value ~ (1|dummy) #no individual differences
    , data = my_data
)
unrestricted_model = lmer(
    formula = VD_value ~ (1|Individual) #individual differences
    , data = my_data
)
bits_of_evidence = (AIC(restricted)-AIC(unrestricted))*log2(exp(1))
print(bits_of_evidence)
# sign reflects whether the unrestricted (+) or restricted (-) model
is supported by the data
# magnitude reflects degree of support

#evaluate evidence for a difference between individual effects of Time
restricted_model = lmer(
    formula = VD_value ~ (1|individual) + Time
    , data = my_data
)
unrestricted_model = lmer(
    formula = VD_value ~ (1+Time|Individual) + Time
    , data = my_data
)
bits_of_evidence = (AIC(restricted)-AIC(unrestricted))*log2(exp(1))
print(bits_of_evidence)

#evaluate evidence for a difference between individual effects of Treatment
restricted_model = lmer(
    formula = VD_value ~ (1|individual) + Treatment
    , data = my_data
)
unrestricted_model = lmer(
    formula = VD_value ~ (1+Treatment|Individual) + Treatment
    , data = my_data
)
bits_of_evidence = (AIC(restricted)-AIC(unrestricted))*log2(exp(1))
print(bits_of_evidence)

#evaluate evidence for a difference between individual Time:Treatment
interactions
restricted_model = lmer(
    formula = VD_value ~ (1+Time+Treatment|individual) +
Time+Treatment+Time:Treatment
    , data = my_data
)
unrestricted_model = lmer(
    formula = VD_value ~ (1+Time+Treatment+Time:Treatment|Individual)
+ Time+Treatment+Time:Treatment
    , data = my_data
)
bits_of_evidence = (AIC(restricted)-AIC(unrestricted))*log2(exp(1))
print(bits_of_evidence)
